title: Circulating factors and their influence on muscle wasting and proteostasis in older adults
summary:
As we age, the risk of sarcopenia (from the Greek “sarx” = “flesh” and “penia” = “lack”) increases dramatically. This term refers to the age-related loss of muscle mass and strength. Studies show that over 20% of people aged 60 to 70 are affected by sarcopenia, and among those aged 75, muscle loss is present in an average of one in two people.
The loss of muscle mass and strength massively increases the risk of falling. The consequences of falls are often accompanied by hospital stays, which can further limit mobility and independence. This results in a reduced quality of life and even life expectancy for those affected.
Consequently, it is of critical importance to prevent the onset of sarcopenia in older adults and to investigate the molecular biological causes of muscle wasting. This will enable the identification of potential therapeutic targets.
The S.A.G.E. study aims to identify various circulating factors in the blood of older adults and investigate their influence on muscle cell growth. To this end, blood samples are taken from older patients in the geriatric ward at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, and additional tests are conducted to assess muscle strength and function. Commercially available muscle cells are then treated in the laboratory with the patients’ blood serum, and various molecules in the blood samples are analyzed. The study participants are divided into five groups: sarcopenic patients, older patients with other conditions (multimorbidity), sarcopenic and multimorbid patients, as well as a younger and an older healthy group for comparison. 
It is expected that the treated muscle cells will shrink more significantly when exposed to blood from sarcopenic patients than when treated with blood from multimorbid patients or healthy older or younger individuals. This would be accompanied by changes in various circulating molecules in the blood that promote muscle loss and inflammatory responses.

interventions.name:
The SAGE study is an observational study involving the following groups:

First, the study includes three groups (each with n = 50) of geriatric patients of all genders:
1. Sarcopenic patients (aged 65 and older)
2.    Multimorbid patients (without sarcopenia) (aged 65 and older)
3.    Sarcopen

Two control groups (each with n = 50) of healthy younger and older participants of all genders are planned:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Geriatric patients: Capacity to give informed consent (through a legal representative if necessary), knowledge of German, 65 years and older
Healthy older participants: No severe or cardiometabolic diseases, BMI 20–30 kg/m², 70 years and older
Healthy younger participants: No chronic diseases, BMI 20–25 kg/m², 18-40 years
Exclusion criteria:
Geriatric patients: Acute delirium, acute sepsis, life expectancy < 3 months as estimated by the attending physician
Healthy elderly participants: Severe or cardiometabolic diseases (type 2 diabetes, heart failure, liver and kidney failure), BMI 20 < and > 30 kg/m²
Young, healthy participants: Chronic diseases, BMI < 20 or > 25 kg/m²
